# Bash Gotchas

> Known bash shell patterns that cause silent failures or unexpected output. Load HIGH entries before writing any bash scripts.

## Entries

- [jq outputs pretty-printed JSON by default -- use -c for JSONL](jq-compact.md): jq -c produces single-line output. Without -c, grep and wc -l fail on multi-line JSON. HIGH.
- [`command -v` finds a Windows Store alias stub that never runs, silently selecting a broken interpreter](command-v-finds-nonexecuting-stub.md): `command -v` answers "does the name resolve", not "can I run it"; on Windows the Microsoft Store app-execution-alias `python3` resolves and exits 0, but running it prints the Store message to stderr and exits 49 with NO stdout, so the python3 branch is taken, every command substitution returns "", and the working jq fallback in the elif is never reached -- in a hook library that parsed every field to "" and silently disabled every gate in the repo. Probe the capability with a stdout sentinel, never presence on PATH; exit-code-only probes are still not enough. HIGH.
- [Git Bash on Windows: PATH and tool availability](git-bash-windows.md): /usr/bin not always on PATH. Use explicit PATH setup or full paths for utilities in scripts and hooks. MEDIUM.
- [gh issue close --comment silently drops the comment on already-closed issues](gh-close-comment-on-already-closed.md): The --comment body is dropped (exit 0) when the issue is already closed. Comment-first, then close. MEDIUM.
- [Verify the current git branch before committing](verify-branch-before-commit.md): With shared working trees a parallel process can move HEAD; your next commit lands on the wrong branch and push says "Everything up-to-date". Check git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD first; push HEAD not a named ref. MEDIUM.
- [A PostToolUse hook that records DB migrations on the ABSENCE of an error](hook-scans-tool-output-false-record.md): Two rounds. First, psql echoes the migration filename in its error output, so a hook grepping the whole payload records failed applies -- parse tool_input.command only. Then the fix for that added a NEGATIVE guard (record unless the output says ERROR:/ROLLBACK), and absence of an error word is not evidence of success: a dry-run that was redirected, quiet (-q), truncated, or produced an empty tool_response reads exactly like a clean apply. Three migrations were stamped whose 23 tables did not exist, and because a forward-only runner selects version > MAX(version), the phantom mark buried four pending migrations while status reported 0. Require positive evidence instead -- psql was handed the file itself via -f/--file/<, a bare COMMIT status line, and the declared objects confirmed present in the DB. HIGH.
- [Fandom wikis: scrape via the MediaWiki API, not the HTML (Cloudflare blocks it)](fandom-mediawiki-api.md): Fandom article HTML sits behind a Cloudflare JS challenge that defeats WebFetch (403) and curl-with-browser-UA alike; use api.php (action=parse / action=query&prop=revisions / list=categorymembers) for raw wikitext instead. MEDIUM.
- [An in-place edit whose anchor does not match changes nothing and exits 0](in-place-edit-no-match-silent-noop.md): sed -i and Python str.replace both treat "anchor not found" as success, so a scripted edit that did nothing is indistinguishable from one that worked; anchoring a version bump on the value being replaced means the first no-op silently disables every later bump, and a paired `echo > VERSION` (which cannot fail) drifts away from it unnoticed. Anchor on shape, assert the file changed, and gate CI on the invariant. HIGH.
- [`comm` can return empty output for every pair, so a set-diff verification passes without comparing anything](comm-silent-empty-output-git-bash.md): Under Git Bash on Windows `comm -12` was observed emitting nothing for every input pair -- including one with a known 19-line intersection, and including under LC_ALL=C with no stderr diagnostic. Because pre-flight safety checks are written as "should be 0", a checker that outputs nothing passes them all and fails OPEN, green-lighting a destructive batch. Use `grep -F -x -f` (fixed strings, whole line, no sort/collation/locale dependency), and ALWAYS pair should-be-zero assertions with a control assertion that must be NON-zero -- otherwise a broken checker is indistinguishable from clean data. HIGH.
- [MSYS path conversion rewrites a leading-slash `jq --arg` value into a Windows path, corrupting every URL inside generated JSON](msys-path-conversion-corrupts-jq-arg.md): Git Bash/MSYS converts any argument starting with `/` into a Windows path before the program sees it, so `jq --arg mb "/users/.../messages"` yields `C:/Program Files/Git/users/.../messages` in every generated URL; jq exits 0 and the JSON is well-formed, so only the generated artifact is wrong while the source data validates clean. Fix with `export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` or prepend the slash inside jq, and verify by reading values back OUT of the generated file. Also `tr -d '\r'` heredoc-written data files on Windows (CRLF). HIGH.
- [A Cloudflare challenge answers HTTP 200 with a body, so a blocked wiki scrape yields an empty digest instead of an error](cloudflare-challenge-200-empty-digest.md): The companion entry's "Fandom blocks HTML but api.php is not challenged" is a per-site WAF setting, not a MediaWiki property -- Bulbapedia challenges `/w/api.php` itself, defeating WebFetch, curl, and curl-with-browser-UA together. It does not look like a failure: HTTP 200, ~6KB written, so `curl -f`, `set -e` and non-empty checks all pass, while the body is `<title>Just a moment...</title>` with zero article content. A tolerant `jq ... // empty` or a tag-strip then returns "" and the caller records "this page has no content", so a 90-page research pass emits a confidently empty result rather than an error. missingtitle and #REDIRECT stubs are 200s too. Assert on body SHAPE (reject a leading doctype, require real length, `jq -e`), fall back to a different HOST not a different path, and prove the detector fires on a known-blocked URL first. HIGH.
